key_insight: The study builds a machine-learning-assisted Cardiology Interface Terminology (CIT) to better highlight important details in cardiology EHR notes.
clinical_relevance: A more complete highlighting system may help clinicians spot key information faster in dense cardiology records and reduce missed details.
method: Started with an initial cardiology terminology from SNOMED, EHR-mined concepts, abbreviations, and medications.
Generated candidate phrases from build-set notes, then semi-automatically reviewed them to create training data (TCIT).
Trained an ML model on TCIT to discover additional concepts and produce the final CIT for test-set highlighting.
evidence_signal: In the test set, the highlighted notes achieved 74.21% coverage and 1.68 breadth; for 20 random notes, average completeness was 98.2% and conciseness was 84.2%.
watch_item: The approach depends on semi-automatic review and training on a specific cardiology dataset, so transferability and maintenance in other specialties or institutions may be limited.
paper_title: Curation of a Cardiology Interface Terminology for Highlighting Electronic Health Records using Machine Learning
